issues.body: `blake2s(generated_at) % len(items)` independently maps each tick to a head position. Nothing ensures that successive valid plan timestamps visit every residue, or even avoid repeating one residue indefinitely. The assertion over 288 timestamps for `len == 10` is only an empirical property of that fixture; it does not establish the advertised property for other queue lengths, time windows, tick schedules, or chosen valid timestamps. In particular, a deterministic sequence can omit a position for an arbitrarily long interval, so a row beyond the capacity cut-off can still starve. The docstring's claim that the change keeps every prior property except starvation, and that expected wait is about `n/c`, is therefore unsupported by the algorithm's actual invariant.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the head from a monotonic plan tick/epoch and use a traversal whose step is guaranteed coprime to the current queue length, or persist a cursor, so every position is reached within a stated bound. Add tests across varied queue lengths and consecutive production tick sequences that assert each position is served within that bound; include lengths sharing factors with the tick interval and mutation probes that repeat or skip a residue. If only probabilistic fairness is intended, narrow the feature claim and explicitly justify why unbounded starvation risk satisfies the source requirement.
issues.title: Timestamp hashing does not guarantee starvation-free service

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 2 fixes the prior delivery-edge finding: `dispatch()` is structurally bound to `review_service_queue(plan, repo)`, and the helper-level tests pin the per-repository partition against empty, global, frozen-repository, and inverted-predicate mutations. However, the new ordering algorithm does not actually provide the claimed starvation freedom. Hashing each timestamp chooses a deterministic pseudo-random head, but it supplies no invariant that every position is reached within any bounded sequence of ticks; the test demonstrates coverage only for one queue length and one hand-picked day. Thus the fixed-head starvation defect has been changed into probabilistic service without a sound bounded-fairness guarantee. Because this is a new major finding, progress is regressing under the required rubric.
